source_name: CRZ entity page – EXIMBANKA SR
why_relevant: Second state-owned banking institution publishing signed contracts in CRZ; a small but clean sample of banking IT/payment supplier relationships with named vendors and prices, and a useful control against SZRB for vendor comparison.

source_name: Ministerstvo financií SR – Zverejňovanie zmlúv, objednávok a faktúr (incl. Štátna pokladnica scope)
why_relevant: MF SR is the parent of Štátna pokladnica, DataCentrum and the state's payment infrastructure; its disclosure hub is the entry point for treasury-side IT, card-acceptance and payment-gateway supplier contracts. Also documents the statutory exemption regime — contracts concluded within Štátna pokladnica's remit relating to financial and payment services are exempt from mandatory publication, which is a material coverage limit to record.

source_name: eGovZmluvy – zmluvy.egov.sk (multi-entity contract publication platform)
why_relevant: Commercial publication platform used by a large number of territorial self-governments, VÚC (e.g. Bratislavský samosprávny kraj, ~21k documents), budgetary organisations and schools to meet the disclosure duty; it also documents its interlinking with CRZ. It aggregates the municipal layer where ATM siting leases, POS acceptance agreements and small IT awards actually appear, and hosts contract PDFs directly (e.g. a Štátna pokladnica current-account contract PDF).

source_name: Bratislavský samosprávny kraj – Otvorená župa / Zmluvy
why_relevant: VÚC-level contract register for the wealthiest Slovak region (TIS ranked it first for disclosure quality). Regional governments contract cash handling, card-acceptance for fee payments, ticketing/POS in transport, and IT — a strong sample of the sub-national buyer layer required by this cell. Mirrored into CRZ under its own entity page.

source_name: Mesto Bratislava – Zmluvy, faktúry, objednávky + zverejnovanie.bratislava.sk
why_relevant: Capital-city disclosure layer covering the city and its subordinate organisations (transport, parking, culture), where card-acceptance, parking payment, ticketing terminals and ATM-space leases are contracted. The separate zverejnovanie.bratislava.sk portal exposes per-IČO subject pages, convenient for vendor-centric queries.

source_name: Mesto Košice – zverejnenie2.esluzbykosice.sk + Open Data Košice (Zmluvy)
why_relevant: Košice publishes all contracts from EUR 0 (above the legal minimum), links each contract to its annexes/amendments and allows search inside individual order line items — unusually granular for unit-price extraction on terminals, ATMs and IT services. An Open Data mirror at opendata.kosice.sk/pages/zmluvy provides machine-readable access. The portal itself is a DATALAN 'Digitálne mesto' deployment, which incidentally identifies a local IT vendor active in the public sector.

source_name: Uvostat – Register zmlúv mirror, detailed search and API
why_relevant: Independent mirror of CRZ (~5.75M contracts, harvested since 2014) with a far better query surface than the official site: cross-field detailed search (supplier, client, subject, number, status, amount, dates), Excel exports of a subject's full profile, and a documented API filterable by contract and by purchaser/vendor IČO. It also joins contracts to public-procurement records, which links a signed contract back to its tender — or shows there was none (direct award), exactly the signal this cell targets.

source_name: Slovensko.Digital platform – CRZ data mirrors / API discussion threads
why_relevant: Community meta-source that catalogues who mirrors CRZ and how: uvostat's API and rate limits, historical bulk CSV (crz_dokumenty.zip, ~1.2M rows of contract names/file URLs/sizes), a torrent-distributed crz.sql.gz SQL dump, and the important caveat that these dumps carry metadata, not the ~1TB of PDF documents. Fastest route to a legal bulk-ingestion strategy without reinventing it, and it snowballs to the wider Slovensko.Digital open-data ecosystem (ekosystem.slovensko.digital).

source_name: OtvorenéZmluvy.sk (Transparency International Slovensko / Aliancia Fair-play)
why_relevant: NGO watchdog portal built on CRZ plus ~130 smaller institutional registers, with detailed contract search, RSS alerts and an eleven-criterion risk scoring that flags missing prices, threshold-hugging amounts and contracts in riskier categories. Valuable both as an alternative index over the same corpus and as a ready-made anomaly filter for direct awards. Only the TIS announcement page was reached in this pass; the otvorenezmluvy.sk application itself did not surface in results and may be dormant — treat as unverified, not dead.

source_name: FinStat.sk – company data with contract/procurement joins
why_relevant: Aggregates ~20 data sources on Slovak companies including the central contract register, public procurement, commercial register and financial statements, with Excel export, monitoring and an API. Essential for turning a contract counterparty string into a resolved legal entity (IČO, ownership, revenue, group links) and for sizing a vendor's public-sector dependency — the entity-resolution layer this cell needs on top of raw contracts.

source_name: Obchodný register SR (orsr.sk) – legal entity verification
why_relevant: Authoritative commercial register used to confirm the exact legal entity, IČO, registered seat and statutory bodies of the vendors and subcontractors named in CRZ contracts — necessary because contracts often name a local subsidiary or a consortium member rather than the recognisable group brand.

source_name: rzof.sk – Register zmlúv, objednávok a faktúr (SMB/municipal publication service)
why_relevant: One of several commercial platforms that small obliged entities (obce, školy, príspevkové organizácie) use to publish contracts. Matters because the long tail of ATM-siting leases and small POS/IT awards is scattered across such platforms rather than CRZ; enumerating the platforms is the way to reach that tail systematically.

source_name: Zverejnovanie.sk – legislation and obliged-entity guidance on contract publication
why_relevant: Reference source on the legal framework of publication duty (211/2000 Z.z., 546/2010 Z.z., 382/2011 Z.z.), including who is an obliged entity and which contract types are exempt. Needed to reason correctly about coverage: an absence in CRZ can mean 'exempt' rather than 'no contract', which materially changes any vendor-share inference.

source_name: CRZ metodika – Metodický pokyn pre zverejňovanie zmlúv v CRZ
why_relevant: Official methodology defining the metadata fields obliged entities must fill (contract number, subject, total price, parties, IČO, dates, annex linkage) and how documents are attached. It is the schema specification for any CRZ ingestion pipeline and explains recurring data-quality defects such as missing prices or free-text subjects that defeat naive keyword search.

source_name: Portál OR SR (sluzby.orsr.sk) — modern commercial register portal / e-services
why_relevant: Newer front-end to the same statutory data, with structured search and issuance of verified extracts; useful when the legacy orsr.sk ASP search is flaky or when an authoritative extract is needed for an entity-resolution decision on a vendor.

source_name: Živnostenský register SR (ŽRSR) — Trade Licensing Register, Ministry of Interior
why_relevant: Covers trade-licence scope (predmety podnikania) for both companies and sole traders. Useful for small SK integrators, ATM/terminal service subcontractors and installers that never appear in vendor marketing but do appear as licensed operators; the licensed activities also hint at what a vendor is actually permitted to deliver.

source_name: Register účtovných závierok (RÚZ) — registeruz.sk
why_relevant: Legally mandated filing of full financial statements (súvaha, výkaz ziskov a strát, poznámky) and annual reports for every Slovak accounting unit from 2013 onward. This is the primary way to size local banking/payments vendors and competitors by revenue (tržby), profit, assets and headcount, and to see the SK P&L of foreign vendors' subsidiaries.

source_name: RÚZ Open API — machine-readable financial statements feed
why_relevant: Documented public API for incremental retrieval of accounting units, financial statements, annual reports and statement line items. Turns the whole SK vendor-financials problem into a structured pipeline instead of scraping, and supports continuous monitoring for new filings by tracked vendors.

source_name: Register partnerov verejného sektora (RPVS) — rpvs.gov.sk
why_relevant: Any vendor receiving public money above thresholds (state banks, ministries, Slovenská pošta, public-sector card/terminal or IT contracts) must register and disclose its konečný užívateľ výhod (ultimate beneficial owner) plus a verification document (verifikačný dokument) written by an oprávnená osoba. The verification documents often narrate the group ownership chain and contract context — unusually rich competitive intelligence for free.

source_name: Ministerstvo spravodlivosti SR — RPVS service page and FAQ
why_relevant: Authoritative explanation of RPVS scope, thresholds and obligations — needed to interpret absences correctly (a vendor missing from RPVS may simply be below threshold, not absent from public contracts). Also links onward to other justice registers.

source_name: Register úpadcov (RÚ) — insolvency, liquidation and pre-insolvency proceedings
why_relevant: Statutory register of konkurz/reštrukturalizácia/likvidácia proceedings, administrators and claim lists. Flags distressed or failing SK vendors and competitors before it shows in filings, and is the place to check counterparty risk for a prospective partner or subcontractor in banking/payments.

source_name: Obchodný vestník SR — official commercial gazette
why_relevant: Daily statutory publication stream: registrations and changes in the commercial register, mergers/splits (zlúčenie, splynutie, rozdelenie), liquidations, bankruptcy notices, convocations of general meetings, and notices of financial-statement deposits. This is the earliest public signal of a vendor acquisition, restructuring or subsidiary set-up in SK banking/payments.

source_name: Foaf.sk — company/person connection graph for Slovakia
why_relevant: Graph-algorithm view over commercial-register and gazette data showing shared directors, shareholders and 'close companies'. The right tool for mapping which SK banking/payments vendors share owners or management, and for detecting shell/holding layers between a foreign vendor and its SK contracting entity.

source_name: RPO — Register právnických osôb, podnikateľov a orgánov verejnej moci (Statistical Office)
why_relevant: Since Nov 2015 the legal single source of identification data for all SK legal persons and entrepreneurs, consolidating 70+ source registers. Best canonical entity-resolution backbone (IČO, legal form, SK NACE main activity, status) for building a vendor/competitor master list before enriching with financials.

source_name: ÚVO — Zoznam hospodárskych subjektov / registers of economic operators
why_relevant: Public Procurement Office registers of qualified economic operators (and the historic register of beneficial owners it maintained before RPVS). Identifies which vendors are formally pre-qualified to bid for SK public/state-bank IT and payments tenders, and links names to IČO for tender-side analysis.

source_name: Ekosystém Slovensko.Digital — Datahub / Prémiové API over Slovak registers
why_relevant: Non-profit-run consolidated API and open datasets combining ORSR, RÚZ, RPVS, tax/VAT and debtor lists into a single normalised company record with IČO/DIČ/IČ DPH. Practical middle path when the state APIs are fragmented and FinStat licensing is not desired.

source_name: Register.peniaze.sk — cross-register aggregator of SK entities and persons
why_relevant: Free consolidated lookup pulling multiple SK registers into one profile (company and person view). Useful as a quick triangulation layer and for person-level searches on vendor directors when ORSR person search is awkward.

source_name: e-Justice / BRIS — EU Business Registers Interconnection, Slovakia entry
why_relevant: EU-level gateway describing and linking the SK commercial and insolvency registers, and enabling cross-border search of parent entities. Essential when a SK payments/banking vendor entity is a subsidiary of an AT/CZ/DE/NL parent and the group chain must be walked outside SK sources.
